title: How Auburn found its magic again by beating No. 1 Georgia at its own game - CBS Sports
description: After enduring five straight losing seasons and 21 years without a win between the hedges, the Tigers delivered t
body:
After enduring five straight losing seasons and 21 years without a win between the hedges, the Tigers delivered their most monumental upset in years
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The last two head coaches at Auburn made promises to return the program to glory but never came close. On Saturday, Alex Golesh completed a mere six-game journey to reignite the magic Auburn had lost. The Tigers knocked off No. 1 Georgia 27-24 between the hedges, perhaps the season's biggest upset, beating the Bulldogs at their own game with bone-rattling physicality. Auburn scored 24 straight points to overcome an early 14-0 deficit, with quarterback Byrum Brown carrying the ball 26 times for 115 yards and the defense forcing three turnovers, including a Gunner Stockton fumble with 58 seconds remaining that set up Alex McPherson for a 34-yard field goal as time expired. Georgia was favored by nearly three touchdowns (-20.5).  "It's detail -- six to eight seconds," Golesh told CBS Sports by phone while riding back on Auburn's victorious team bus. "It's strain. Six to eight seconds. One play at a time. That's really hard to believe until you actually can wrap your mind around it. It's a mindset. It's the only way to go and play in an environment like that and be able to win that game." The relentless, weekly physical toll of playing in the SEC is undeniable. Coming off their monumental, exhausting clash in Tuscaloosa just a week earlier, both Alabama and Georgia fell on Saturday. Undeniably, the resulting aches and fatigue contributed to both the Crimson Tide and the Bulldogs dropping games on the very same day. "Like I say, humility is a week away," Georgia's Kirby Smart told reporters after the loss, the second largest upset of his career (barely behind a loss to South Carolina in 2019).  
"This was the seventh week in a row for those guys," Golesh said. "We were fortunate to be able to come off a bye week. It's just part of it." But the story here isn't Georgia or the AP's No. 1 team falling in back-to-back weeks for the first time in 36 years. Saturday belonged to the resurrected calls of "War Eagle!" and the electric celebrations at Toomer's Corner, where fans gather on the edge of campus to roll the oak trees with toilet paper to mark victories. Long considered the SEC's most magical program, Auburn's ability to beat top-5 programs and win conference and national championships remains extraordinary -- especially as it is geographically sandwiched between Alabama during Nick Saban's unprecedented modern dynasty and Georgia as Smart hit his championship stride. Truth be told, the five straight losing seasons since 2021 on the Plains should be less surprising than their magical, memorable and historic runs in 2010 (national title), 2013 (SEC championship), and 2017 (wins over No. 1 Alabama and No. 1 Georgia). 
Winning is hard. Doing it against two rivals in their golden eras should be darn near impossible. Auburn's long road: Every season record since last win vs. UGA (2017)   SeasonAuburn record201710-420188-520199-420206-520216-720225-720236-720245-720255-720264-2 (through Oct. 17)One of the first things Golesh shared after beating Georgia was the encouraging messages he received from former Auburn players Takeo Spikes and Jason Campbell before kickoff. Fan and former player support is unbreakable, but Auburn's worst five-year stretch since the 1940s tested their resolve."Our fan base has been through a lot," Golesh said on ESPN after the game. "We're going to build Auburn back to where everybody wants it – one game at a time. Just hang with us." 
Auburn has been lost in the wilderness since 2021. Bryan Harsin and Hugh Freeze combined for a 24-31 record during that stretch, with Harsin's era particularly poor. Auburn entered Saturday on a 12-game road losing streak against ranked opponents, the second-worst mark in school history. Heck, Auburn hadn't scored multiple touchdowns at Georgia since 2009 and the Tigers hadn't won there since 2005. They were in danger of losing a 10th straight in The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry, potentially the longest losing streak in the series' history. Take it from Gus Malzahn, the last coach to record a winning season on the Plains in 2020, his final season. He led Auburn to a national title as an offensive coordinator and an SEC championship as head coach, but never defeated Georgia between the hedges in his eight seasons leading the Tigers. His offense scored multiple touchdowns in Athens only once, in his first season as offensive coordinator, which was also a loss. 
"I'm just really happy for the Auburn fans. Everything they've went through the last five years, man, I'm just really happy for them. They needed that," Malzahn told CBS Sports. "That was a huge deal. It's hard to not just beat a No. 1 team, but on the road, especially at that place? Unbelievably impressive. Great job by Golesh and his staff, because I know how hard it is to win there. Big-time win." Whether Auburn is back on the map is an argument for another day. The Tigers certainly appear primed to return to the postseason this fall. The building blocks also appear in place for a return to the top half of the SEC next season, with a solid NIL budget, a promising recruiting class and a strong base of talent already on campus. On Saturday night, the Auburn faithful descended on Toomer's Corner en masse to celebrate its biggest win in seven years. They closed the intersection of College Street and Magnolia Avenue as fans stood shoulder to shoulder, packed together in downtown Auburn. They call themselves the "Auburn Family," a moniker ridiculed outside eastern Alabama, but true for all who live and breathe it. 
For Golesh, most of his family was back home for his daughter's Homecoming festivities. His wife called Saturday night to tell him Auburn fans had rolled their house with toilet paper. "Only in Auburn do people know where you live," Golesh told reporters. His son, Bear, didn't stay behind. On Thursday, he asked his father, the Auburn head coach, a question. "Dad, can I get on the field after we win?" Golesh said on ESPN after the game, fighting back tears.  
"I mean, he's getting his ass ripped for not making his bed," Golesh told CBS Sports later. "And all he cared about is, can I be on the field after we win?" He looked at his son on the field and pulled him in tight with his left arm.  "We're on the field, bro." Saturday's monumental upset was the first time an unranked team beat a No. 1 on the road since 2007. In the future, Golesh hopes it's just another win on the road to a championship for an Auburn program that hasn't finished in the top 25 since 2019 or appeared in the SEC Championship Game since 2017. Heading into Saturday, Auburn was tagged as a three-touchdown underdog facing a Georgia program that had strung together 53 consecutive wins against unranked opponents. Yet the Tigers pulled it off, rallying from a 14-point deficit to something an unranked team hadn't done since 1998 -- when, strangely enough, Nick Saban guided Michigan State to a stunning rally to beat No. 1 Ohio State as an unranked squad. 
Not many saw this coming. Golesh's son apparently did. "I believed him," Golesh told CBS Sports. "I get emotional on that simply because nobody gives you a chance, and then your 12-year-old son actually believes that you can go win that game. As neat as that is, it's such a true story." Auburn's magic is back.

schema.headline: How Auburn found its magic again by beating No. 1 Georgia at its own game - CBS Sports

title: How the Washington Spirit found their playoff form in a gritty 1-0 win over NWSL rivals Gotham FC - CBS Sports
description: Lucia Di Guglielmo's first league goal secured a 1-0 victory over first-place Gotham FC at Audi Field, halting th
body:
Lucia Di Guglielmo's first league goal secured a 1-0 victory over first-place Gotham FC at Audi Field, halting the reigning champions from locking up the regular-season crown
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Washington Spirit punched their ticket to the 2026 NWSL playoffs, and the NWSL Shield just got more interesting. The Spirit defeated Gotham FC, the reigning NWSL Championship winners, 1-0, at Audi Field on Saturday.The two teams gave audiences a glimpse of playoff-caliber action, with high stakes. Gotham FC leads the league table with 55 points but has not yet clinched the NWSL Shield, and the loss means they'll have to try again next weekend. The win keeps Washington Spirit in contention for the NWSL Shield and marks the club's third consecutive postseason return since Michelle Kang's takeover in 2022. Newly acquired Lucia Di Guglielmo scored the decisive goal; it's the Italian international's first NWSL goal and the Spirit's first against Gotham since November 2024, during the 2024 NWSL semifinals.Spirit spoil Gotham's shield partyThe win carries big implications, and the way the Spirit spoiled Gotham's form and clinched a playoff spot says even more. The scene setter for the Spirit wasn't hard to miss, as Audi Field is often referred to as "rowdy," and consistent effort earns cheers as loud as goals.
Gotham's injury woes appeared to catch up to them with rookie Jordynn Dudley out for the season with a foot fracture, and Jaedyn Shaw as an unused sub. Shaw left USWNT U23 camps early as a precaution following an injury, and was not listed as unavailable for Saturday's match, but was not utilized after warming up at various points of the match. But ultimately, the reigning champions have a deep bench and couldn't generate more offense despite having more of the ball. Even with a deliberate game plan by Spirit head coach Adrian Gonzalez to absorb more and have less of the ball by design, the Spirit created more shots (13) and more shots on target (six) than Gotham despite losing the possession battle. 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            "Today [it] was key to be very compact, narrow, protecting the middle a lot. And then I think we've done a good job with Esme [Morgan] with T [Rudd] stepping, jumping to those pockets, and not allowing them to receive comfortably there," Gonzalez said after the game.
"Overall, the team I think has done a great job at different heights. I think, pressing high, forcing them to play long. Anytime that they wanted to play back, I think we've stepped really good, making their attack more uncomfortable. And in a mid-low block situation, I think the team has defended pretty good."Spirit midfield is healingFrom newly acquired players to long-time members of the Spirit, it felt like a turning of the page for the Spirit into a mode of the season they aren't unfamiliar with; the playoff grind.Tanzania international Clara Luvanga wasn't on the score sheet but was a constant mark for Gotham in the final third, with her hold-up play, distributing the ball wide, and being a threat on goal in the first half. Team captain and Spirit veteran Andi Sullivan is back from maternity leave, getting starting minutes again, and the return of Leicy Santos, even on a minutes restriction, reminded everyone why she was such a missed piece of the equation while on the injury list. 
"Obviously we've missed her, all of us. It's been a process, and we've tried to be very cautious and prudent, especially not to push her too hard, because she's accumulated a lot of minutes with us and with the national team. It was especially important for her to reach this final stretch in optimal condition so she could help us, without making the mistake of trying to bring her back too quickly," Gonzalez said."She was ready to play 45 minutes today, and I think she gave the team a lot. Once again, she showed her talent. Even after being out for a long time, she has the ability to make an impact in a game like this. In 45 minutes, she showed her quality on the ball, her ability to find the final pass, and her personality in competing and defending. She brings us a great deal. Going forward, we'll continue to be cautious, make sure her progress is right, and gradually see how she settles back in. We'll try to add minutes little by little, knowing that we still have several matches ahead."Santo's minutes restriction opened the door for Melissa Bethi to have her own impact on the game. The Algerian international was acquired midseason and joined the team following the Women's African Cup of Nations and delivered the game-winning assist to Di Guglielmo.
"I mean, it's like a dream, or even more, because it's kind of the perfect situation, the perfect first goal, perfect win, and everything is special here," Di Guglielmo said after the game.NWSL Shield race heats upWhile Saturday's win clinched another playoff appearance for the Spirit, it also keeps them in the mix for the NWSL Shield. It's one of the more interesting races in league history, as three teams, including the San Diego Wave, are in the hunt with just a few games remaining. The Spirit aren't getting ahead of themselves, though, as Sullivan knows anything can happen and there's always work to be done.  "I'm still focused on this next regular season game; I think that's the attitude we need to have. I think there can be a lot of like narratives about the past two seasons and playoffs and everything, but the most important thing is the week in front of you and putting yourself and your team in the best situation to win the game in front of you ... because you know you can't get too far ahead of yourself too early," Sullivan said.  "That's kind of the messaging that I'll be spreading to the team, and I think that's something that we can always improve on is focusing on the task at hand."

schema.headline: How the Washington Spirit found their playoff form in a gritty 1-0 win over NWSL rivals Gotham FC - CBS Sports

title: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide season - CBS Sports
description: With the Buckeyes' star quarterback out "several weeks," and challenging Big Ten opponents on deck, the trajector
body:
With the Buckeyes' star quarterback out "several weeks," and challenging Big Ten opponents on deck, the trajectory of Ohio State's season is very much up in the air
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana, a game neither team escaped feeling whole.Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride.
But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking.That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. 
After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt.The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program.Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks."

        
            
                Ohio State QB Julian Sayin to miss 'several weeks' after suffering injury in win vs. Indiana
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC, and then it's a home game with Oregon. While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray.If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State, as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too.While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

schema.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide season - CBS Sports

title: Big 12 rules Notre Dame should have been allowed another play after officiating error in loss to BYU - CBS Sports
description: The clock still had :01 remaining when officials erroneous
body:
The clock still had :01 remaining when officials erroneously ruled the Cougars-Irish game was over
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:56 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        While most of America was wondering whether pass interference should have been called on BYU at the end of the No. 8 Cougars' 28-24 victory vs. No. 2 Notre Dame on Saturday, another college football officiating gaffe was hiding in plain sight if anyone took the time in the moment to look.The Irish needed a touchdown on the game's final play to defeat the Cougars, but CJ Carr's heave to Jade Greathouse fell to the turf on the end zone as officials signaled the end of the game after a brief discussion and BYU fans stormed the field at Lavell Edwards Stadium. But, the party may have started prematurely as the Big 12 admitted an officiating error there should have been :01 remaining on the clock.According to a statement from the Big 12 releaed early Sunday morning, Notre Dame should have had a chance to run another play after the game indeed prematurely. 
"Following the Big 12's review of the final play of Saturday's Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew. The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games."Add it to the pile of clock gaffes in football during the 2026 season. In Week 1, Michigan was given an additional second to complete a Hail Mary, which they did, to rip the heart out of Western Michigan and momentarily save face from an embarrassing moment. This is much more egregious, as there is no doubt if there was time remaining. 
What's unclear is how the College Football Playoff Committee will take this into account when viewing Notre Dame or BYU's cases later this season in how they attempt to set the field.

schema.headline: Big 12 rules Notre Dame should have been allowed another play after officiating error in loss to BYU - CBS Sports

title: 'This team is gonna find a way': How Valkyries shut down Dream in the clutch to take Game 1 of WNBA Finals - CBS Sports
description: The Valkyries came away with a 68-64 win despite shooting just 32.1%
body:
The Valkyries came away with a 68-64 win despite shooting just 32.1%
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:52 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        SAN FRANCISCO -- Still sporting his lavender "Ballhalla" shirt, Joe Lacob stood in the tunnel behind the Chase Center court late on Saturday afternoon, rehashing an extremely physical and competitive Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals. "We didn't play well," the Golden State Valkyries owner was overheard saying. But he wasn't lamenting a loss. He was celebrating his team's 68-64 comeback win over the Atlanta Dream. The Valkyries fell behind on the opening possession, trailed by nine early and again by seven in the fourth quarter. They led for just six minutes and four seconds all day, and shot 32.1%, which was the third-worst field goal percentage in a Finals win in league history. By any objective measure, they did not play well – certainly not on the offensive end. But one of the Valkyries' many mystical qualities is that they don't have to play well in order to win. "Whatever happens, this team is gonna find a way," Gabby Williams said. The Valkyries found a way Saturday in quintessential fashion by leaning on their depth, defense and deafening home-court advantage. 
The pre-game experience at Ballhalla is unique. Not just because of the noise or the light show or the hype video depicting Norse warriors doing battle. When it's time for player introductions, the voice echoing around the arena makes no mention of starters. Rather, "it's time to meet the first five." The Valkyries have "strength in numbers," coach Natalie Nakase said, echoing the mantra that Steve Kerr made famous during the Golden State Warriors' run to the 2015 NBA championship. (Kerr was in attendance Saturday, along with a number of Warriors players.) The Valkyries' "first five" is just that. Whenever they check out, a new wave enters. Nakase went with a 10-player rotation in Game 1; many teams don't go that deep in the regular season. Only two Valkyries players reached 30 minutes, and one of them was Kaila Charles, who came off the bench to put up seven points, a team-high 10 rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block. She had a huge 3-pointer late in the third quarter, and an even bigger steal and layup in the middle of the fourth to end a two-minute scoring drought. It was only right that she grabbed the game-sealing rebound and had the ball as time expired. 
"Her engine was on full throttle tonight," Nakase said. "She emptied the tank the minute she stepped on the floor. You could feel her and you could feel when I took her out … Her fight was unmatched tonight. She's exactly what we needed."Charles' big night was unexpected, but she had at least been in the playoff rotation. Laeticia Amihere, on the other hand, had only played six minutes in the postseason before she checked in with 4:36 in the second quarter with a remit to slow down Angel Reese. To that point, Reese had 14 points and was having her way when Kiah Stokes was out of the game. After Amihere entered the game, Reese didn't score again. In fact, Reese only took three more shots; Amihere blocked one of them and strongly contested another. To go with that rejection, she added five points, five rebounds and a steal. "That's what we are all year. Be ready, be ready when your name is called. I thought LA was phenomenal," Veronica Burton said. "This matchup for her is really good. She knows what she brings to the table and I'm just really proud of her." 
Amihere's effort against Reese was just part of the Valkyries' smothering defensive performance. Allisha Gray, who was playing through a hand injury that had kept her out of the majority of the semifinals, went 5 of 19, Rhyne Howard was 3 of 14 and the Dream shot 32.8% as a team, including 4 of 25 from 3-point range. The Dream, normally so secure with the ball, turned it over 12 times, which led to 17 Valkyries points. In the fourth quarter, with the pressure mounting and the Ballhalla crowd surging, the Valkyries turned things up to another level. They held the Dream to eight points on 2 of 17 from the field. Atlanta's only make over the final 7:16 was an absurd double-clutch leaner off the glass from Jordin Canada to beat the shot clock. As the Dream tried and failed to find any semblance of offense down the stretch, their seven-point lead slowly melted away until Gabby Williams hit two free throws to put the Valkyries in front for good with 1:18 left. 
"Even though we were down with a few minutes left, we had the game right where we wanted it because it just came down to getting stops," Williams said. "That's been our bread and butter all season. That's why we harp on it so much because we've built great defensive habits for these moments."After the Valkyries' final stop in the closing seconds, Lacob and a sea of lavender 18,000 strong erupted. The Valkyries hadn't played well, but they had won. Nakase, who called for "hostility" from the crowd earlier in the week, said she felt a "different roar" on Saturday, but made it clear that even the fans have to "level up" on Monday if the Valkyries want to take a commanding 2-0 lead. "Game 2 it has to be better," Nakase said. "We're gonna ask more from our players, so check for Game 1, let's get a better Game 2. Rest and recover, Ballhalla. Careful what you drink tonight."

schema.headline: 'This team is gonna find a way': How Valkyries shut down Dream in the clutch to take Game 1 of WNBA Finals - CBS Sports

title: Knicks finalize roster as James Wiseman gets last spot over Bruce Brown - CBS Sports
description: Wiseman, a former No. 2 overall pick, will provide frontcourt depth for the reigning NBA champs
body:
Wiseman, a former No. 2 overall pick, will provide frontcourt depth for the reigning NBA champs
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Knicks finalized their roster heading into the 2026-27 season on Saturday, waiving veteran Bruce Brown in order to retain former No. 2 overall pick James Wiseman on the regular season roster. Wiseman has been featured regularly in the Knicks preseason games, averaging 8.0 points and 4.3 rebounds in four appearances in the preseason. After seeing Mitchell Robinson walk in free agency to the rival Boston Celtics, New York needed to bolster its center rotation behind Karl-Anthony Towns. The Knicks signed Andre Drummond in free agency to be their new backup, but needed additional depth and brought in Wiseman on an Exhibit 9 deal (training camp contract), which they'll now convert into a league minimum deal that gets Wiseman back onto a roster with a chance to contribute for the first time in a few years. 
Wiseman played in just five games the last two seasons in Indiana, and while he'll be reserve depth in New York, he could see some regular-season action as they look to be mindful of minutes coming off of a championship run. 
The former No. 2 pick of the Warriors has not been a regular rotation player since 2023-24 in Detroit, when he averaged 7.1 points and 5.3 rebounds per game in 63 appearances. Wiseman was part of the Warriors' initial plans to try and build for the future while competing in the present, but he struggled to produce at a high level and has had defensive woes since entering the league. The Knicks will hope he can provide some size in reserve when called upon for spot duty this season after impressing Mike Brown enough in the preseason to keep him on the roster. 
For Brown, he'll hope to find an opportunity elsewhere after being waived. Brown played in all 82 games a season ago with the Denver Nuggets, averaging 7.9 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.

schema.headline: Knicks finalize roster as James Wiseman gets last spot over Bruce Brown - CBS Sports

title: Miami survives Florida State after disputed Hail Mary INT ends double-OT classic - CBS Sports
description: No. 3 Miami escaped disaster, thanks to clutch plays in overtime and a controversial ruling at the end
body:
No. 3 Miami escaped disaster, thanks to clutch plays in overtime and a controversial ruling at the end
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:13 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The rivalry between Miami and Florida State rarely lacks drama, but Saturday night took the theatrics to another level. The No. 3 Hurricanes narrowly escaped the Seminoles, 43-35, with a wild and controversial finish that will be talked about for years to come.The game was wild enough up to the point at which Miami took an eight-point lead to begin the second overtime, but the final sequence will be debate fodder between the fan bases for quite a while.On fourth-and-21, Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels just launched a jump ball into the end zone, and Seminoles receiver Micahi Danzy came down with it in the midst of a couple of Miami defenders. The Noles hardly had time to celebrate before they noticed laundry in the backfield.Offensive lineman Xavier Chaplin got called for holding, a penalty that rarely gets called in desperate end-of-game situations. Chaplin appeared to get outside the defender's shoulder pads slightly, but the Canes pass-rusher seemed to slip and fall shortly thereafter.
It was a tight call that negated a Seminoles miracle.
With Florida State now facing fourth-and-31, surely it couldn't replicate that magic on a second play? Seminoles fans will argue that they did.Daniels rolled out to his right and threw up a Hail Mary. This time, it was Duce Robinson who leaped up above the pack and got his fingertips on the ball. Miami defensive back Bryce Fitzgerald got his hands on the ball at the same time, and they went to the ground in a scrum.It was hard to tell who had possession, but the officials ruled that it was an interception on the field. After review, they determined that there wasn't enough evidence to overturn that call. ESPN rules analyst Steve Shaw said the ACC officials got it right.
"That was an interception. Clearly nothing to overturn it," Shaw said. "That was the correct call."Mike Norvell disagrees with callsAs you might expect, Florida State coach Norvell didn't agree with the officials or Shaw's assessment. Based on what he saw, Robinson and Fitzgerald got possession simultaneously, which would result in a catch for the Seminoles."I didn't get a whole lot of explanation," Norvell said. "You have a holding call on the play before, and then I watched it, if there's a tie it goes to the receiver. I guess they had a different angle where you could see something different."
When asked about the penalty on Chaplin that negated the first Hail Mary, Norvell stopped just short of saying it was a phantom holding call, but he made his feelings clear."The holding call on the play before, they said it was on No. 77," Norvell said. "Go watch the film."In an odd turn, Norvell also pointed out that this officiating crew was the same one that called last year's game, which ended in a 28-22 win for Miami. The Seminoles attempted an onside kick to keep their late rally alive, but it was recovered by the Hurricanes.
"Pretty unique when you have the same crew back-to-back years in game-ending situations that go down to the last play," Norvell said.Norvell added that he was proud of the way his team fought against a quality opponent, but he was disappointed that the game ended the way it did."It's unfortunate to see guys go out there and perform the way they did," Norvell said. "There's plenty of plays, but to have that outcome come down to a play like that, I'm grateful for our guys and the way they battled."

title: The Spurs will start Dylan Harper on opening night, so where does that leave De'Aaron Fox? - CBS Sports
description: The Spurs will try out a three-guard lineup again at the start of this season with Harper, Fox and Stephon Castle
body:
The Spurs will try out a three-guard lineup again at the start of this season with Harper, Fox and Stephon Castle
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For opening night, at least, the San Antonio Spurs have answered the single biggest starting lineup question of the 2026-27 season. Dylan Harper, the No. 2 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft and the second-best player in San Antonio's NBA Finals loss to the New York Knicks, will officially join the starting five alongside Victor Wembanyama, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell... and De'Aaron Fox, the expensive veteran whose injured ankle and ensuing struggles loomed large over that Finals defeat.San Antonio barely used the three-guard lineup last season, and for good reason. It was outscored significantly in both 54-possession regular-season and 83-possession postseason samples last year. The lineup outscored the Phoenix Suns by 10 points in 25 possessions in a recent preseason victory, but the Spurs shot just 2 of 9 on 3s when all three guards played together in that game.That is the primary concern here. Harper, Fox and Castle are all strong drivers with questionable 3-point shots. Such players typically do best when surrounded by other shooters. The Spurs can get away with having two of them on the floor at once because their center, Victor Wembanyama, is game-breaking in dozens of ways, including his ability to space the floor. San Antonio took off last season when it upgraded its shooting by inserting Julian Champagnie into the starting lineup.With all three guards playing together, though, the delicate balance between shooting and ball-handling has tilted too far toward the latter. Ball-handling doesn't have nearly the amplifying effect that shooting does, and opponents will inevitably cheat off of the two guards without the ball in their hands whenever one of them is trying to create shots with it. The trio is so talented, and comes with the inherent advantage of playing with Wembanyama, that the Spurs will almost certainly win most of the games it plays with this starting lineup. 

        
            
                Ranking the NBA's top 100 players: Victor Wembanyama enters 2026-27 season at No. 1
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
But it's certainly suboptimal. We all know where this is probably heading. Harper was simply too good to keep coming off of the bench, and Castle is too good to ever move there. Eventually, the best version of the Spurs likely has Fox, the oldest and most expensive of the three guards, coming off of the bench as Harper did a season ago. San Antonio's starters with Champagnie playing alongside two of the guards outscored opponents by 17.6 points per 100 possessions a season ago. The formula of two guards, two shooters and Wembanyama is this team's endgame.Yet even if that's the case, the Spurs are slow-playing this. In the long run, that's probably the sensible approach. Benching a reigning All-Star on a max contract is fraught. Fox very intentionally steered himself to San Antonio through a direct trade request, presumably expecting to be the starting point guard on a dynasty. Players of his stature and age are rarely eager to come off of the bench. Asking him to do so on opening night based off of a poor Finals series in which he was injured risks alienating a key player and, cynically, destroying what little trade value he might have left.Even if the Spurs do plan to bench Fox down the line, easing him into it seems like the safest approach. He still has a chance to prove that this three-guard lineup can work, and if it does, well, maybe there's less of a problem here than we're assuming. If it proves uncomfortable or if the lineup data suggests it's flopping, the Spurs at least have empirical data supporting a change. They can at least tell Fox that they tried.
They'd hardly be the first team to try this approach to benching a star. Russell Westbrook went through it with both Los Angeles teams, for instance. The Lakers benched him after an 0-3 start in the 2022-23 season. The Clippers let him and James Harden start five games together a year later, lost all five, and then went 27-7 in their next 34 after benching him. Sometimes, you have to sacrifice a few games for the greater good. Players of this caliber tend to expect a certain degree of respect that the attempt at least affords.The notion of sacrificing games is going to be a bitter pill to swallow in this case, specifically, because San Antonio's competition for the No. 1 seed in the Western Conference practically never does so. The Oklahoma City Thunder churn out 60-win seasons in their sleep, and home-court advantage in the practically preordained Western Conference Finals between them, despite San Antonio's road victory a year ago, is meaningful. But that same road victory showed the Spurs that what matters isn't October or November. It's May and June. If the Spurs have to take the long road to optimized lineups and locker room harmony, so be it. For now, they're giving Harper the starting job he so clearly deserves and tabling the Fox end of the equation until the issue is forced.

title: Michigan benches QB Bryce Underwood to start second half vs. Penn State - CBS Sports
description: Kyle Whittingham sat Underwood, a former five-star recruit, after a scoreless first half against Penn State on Sa
body:
Kyle Whittingham sat Underwood, a former five-star recruit, after a scoreless first half against Penn State on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:02 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Pressed to bench Bryce Underwood as Michigan's starting quarterback throughout this season, Kyle Whittingham finally made the call to sit him to start the second half of Saturday's game against Penn State.After failing to score over the first two quarters with countless empty possessions dictated by faulty execution, two interceptions and several short-armed throws from the five-star sophomore, Michigan went to the bench in favor of freshman Tommy Carr.The Wolverines scored their first points on Carr's second possession thanks to Bryson Kuzdzal's 43-yard touchdown run after Penn State lost containment on the outside. Earlier this week, Michigan offensive coordinator Jason Beck addressed Underwood and the expectations upon the former No. 1 QB recruit.
"Nothing's ever good enough, let alone when it's not going great, right? You always want to play better," Beck said. "There are always things to improve, there are always things to do better. The thing I'll say with Bryce is he cares, and he works hard. It matters to him, and he's feeling that outside noise and all that as much as anybody. He's really handling that well with his approach and the teammate he is, so we're always working to get better and improve."Carr, a former four-star signee and the grandson of former Wolverines coach Lloyd Carr, appeared in only one game previously this season, completing both passes he threw against UTEP.
Carr's older brother is Heisman Trophy candidate and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr.

title: Jalen Hurts blood clot: Expert weighs in on Eagles' situation, and when QB could return to the field - CBS Sports
description: A cardiologist weighs in on how Hurts' condition contrasts with DVTs, standard treatment methods and what could d
body:
A cardiologist weighs in on how Hurts' condition contrasts with DVTs, standard treatment methods and what could determine the recovery timeline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Jalen Hurts' 2026 season was put on pause this week, as the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot that had experienced some movement and the team placed him on IR on Saturday.The team diagnosed the clot and informed the league of Hurts' situation last week, but he was cleared to suit up and play in their Week 5 London loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. After a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the clot, the team announced that Hurts would have to sit out for at least one week while they treated him. It initially looked like the quarterback would avoid injured reserve, but ESPN reported Saturday afternoon that after consultations with doctors and experts, the Eagles decided to place Hurts on injured reserve -- meaning he will miss at least the next four games. What is a superficial blood clot and how much time could Hurts miss? CBS Sports spoke to Dr. Henry Han at UT Southwestern to get some answers. Dr. Han is a board certified cardiologist that works at the intersection of cardiology and vascular medicine. He has seen clot-related diseases, diseases related to aneurysms, tears in blood vessels, and is very familiar with superficial vein thrombosis.What exactly is Jalen Hurts dealing with?A superficial blood clot could be classified as "superficial thrombophlebitis," or a much easier term: "superficial vein thrombosis." 
Dr. Han: "Basically it's a blood clot that's in one of the veins that's on the surface level underneath the skin. We typically find it in the leg, sometimes we find it in the arm. What happens is when the clot forms there, the vein gets inflamed. And so the area turns really red, it gets warm and it gets tender."What's the difference between a superficial clot and the 'deep vein thrombosis' (DVT) that we've seen in sports? This is a situation that deserves monitoring, but it's also not the more serious "deep vein thrombosis" we've seen in sports before. Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama, for example, was forced to miss the final 30 games of the 2024-25 season after doctors discovered deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder. Then there's two-time NBA champion Chris Bosh, who was forced to retire early due to a clotting condition. Dr. Han: "Superficial clots that sit near the surface on your surface veins are a lot less dangerous compared to the DVT (deep vein thrombosis). In sports we hear about the DVTs that for some athletes end up being sort of career-enders. The interesting part is that the superficial vein thromboses typically are not dangerous to that degree and the treatment for what you would need for both is a little bit different as well."
What exactly caused this?In their statement released on Thursday, the Eagles said that four days after the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, Hurts requested treatment on his calf. He believed he was kicked or cleated in the game.It's true that trauma to the area could have caused this clot, but we simply don't have enough information to say that definitively. Dr. Han: "I can't speak to the exact specific case, but sort of generalities, anything that irritates a vein or slows the blood flow can trigger it. So we actually see this for people who have gotten IVs or blood draws when you have a needle in the vein that causes the irritation and damage. Other things too, like long flights. We know that certain hormone medications, pregnancy for women. But definitely trauma is one of the major causes that can cause this sort of superficial thrombophlebitis."
What are the treatment options?There are numerous cases of NFL players missing time due to blood clots. Take Carolina Panthers star right tackle Taylor Moton for example, who hasn't played at all this season because doctors found blood clots in his lung this summer. That situation required Moton to immediately be placed on blood thinners. Moton having blood clots found in one of his lungs is a much more serious situation than superficial thrombophlebitis. It varies case to case, of course, but treatments for what Hurts has been diagnosed with can sometimes be simple. Dr. Han: "Usually what we end up doing for standard of care is that within the first week, you can actually for a lot of patients and a lot of people, you can actually do conservative treatment, which involves things like anti-inflammatory medications, things like ibuprofen or naproxen, staying active, keeping the leg elevated, compression as sort of the first line. 
"In these kinds of situations, we actually often think that the superficial thrombophlebitis is a self-contained issue. Usually what I do for my patients is that we do a follow-up scan either 7 or 14 days after the fact.  And if we see that the quality of the clot has changed, whether the clot is extended or it has moved or we do find it in deeper veins, then that kind of changes the equation for being more aggressive with treatments, which would include things as we typically do for deep vein thrombosis, the DVTs. That would be the full-on blood thinners, anticoagulants." So, could Hurts require blood thinners? Dr. Han: "If it's for superficial thrombophlebitis, not every case needs to be treated with blood thinners. The cases that I treat with blood thinners are for patients that are have the clots that are getting longer or building up, so to speak, or if the patients are profoundly symptomatic with lots of pain that ibuprofen and warm compresses and elevating legs and wearing a compression garment is not cutting it. For those patients, then we do often think about reaching towards anticoagulants, blood thinners. Although the period for treatment for superficial thrombophlebitis is actually much shorter than what we would treat for DVTs. The treatment here is usually a month and a half, 45 days of treatment is sufficient, whereas the DVT sometimes is lifelong, sometimes it's between three to six months."When could Hurts return?Everyone wants to know: when could the Eagles quarterback return to the field? Since this is not a worst-case scenario like deep vein thrombosis, we asked Dr. Han before Hurts was placed on injured reserve if there was any chance he could miss just one or two weeks
Two key factors are whether he requires blood thinners and whether this clot is indeed a self-contained issue.Dr. Han: "It is possible. Again, just because I don't know the details of the case. The risk as I see it is being on a blood thinner and playing a contact sport would put him at extremely high risk of bleeding. And that's all bleeding complications -- blood trauma, but also internal bleeding. Oftentimes for athletics to this degree, it becomes a very strong safety consideration for being able to play or not. It's also a little hard for me to speculate if their phrasing for it -- 'It's moving' -- means that there are clots in other places, then the timeline for when he might come back is a lot harder for me to say."I would say the standard is if he was on blood thinners for just superficial thrombophlebitis that could be -- for symptomatic treatment -- that could be upwards of 45 days for treatment. But if there are extenuating circumstances that would have progressed or made it more dangerous or had turned into a deep vein thrombosis or something like that, then the treatment times could be much longer."

title: How good can Barcelona be? Eleven wins straight and counting to start the season - CBS Sports
description: With 39 goals in nine league games and Lamine Yamal ascending to another level, Hansi Flick's squad has built an
body:
With 39 goals in nine league games and Lamine Yamal ascending to another level, Hansi Flick's squad has built an unstoppable juggernaut
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's 11 matches, 11 wins as Hansi Flick's Barcelona continue their perfect start to the season by defeating Real Betis 5-2. Who else but Lamine Yamal opened the scoring? In his age-19 season, he's taking a step forward despite already being a global superstar, which is scary for the rest of the world.  Flick's men have dispatched every team in their path, and even that level of dominance doesn't do justice to what Barcelona have done this season. Barcelona executed their summer transfers to perfection, and while it's too early to begin discussing a perfect season, it's clear that they have the best attack in the world, and it isn't particularly close. Raphinha missed their last three matches due to injury, and the club didn't miss his 14 goals in all competitions, winning each match by three goals.  It was slightly tougher facing Manuel Pellegrini's Real Betis, but if a team has to score four goals to have a chance of beating Barcelona this season, it brings an immense amount of pressure. Betis are off to an excellent start to the season with six wins in nine LaLiga matches, but they've scored 23 fewer goals than Barcelona. Yes, you read that correctly: 23 fewer goals. In fact, no LaLiga team has come within 20 goals of matching Barcelona's 39 goals in nine games.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            While they've gotten off to an impressive start to the season, it's also worth looking at how they've done it.Hitting the mark on transfersOver the summer, Barcelona added Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Gabriel Jesus and Rodri as they've finally gotten to a point where they can spend money again. Not only have the new attackers added speed in transition, but Rodri has also marshaled the defense so the squad is caught out in transition less often. Those new signings have also accounted for seven LaLiga goals between them and have also given Flick serious depth to rotate while also competing on multiple fronts.  While it's true Barcelona are still conceding goals with Rodri in midfield due to their open play style, only five teams have conceded fewer goals than Barcelona, they don't need to have a stout defense, just one that's good enough to let their historic attack go to work. Keeping things in line is what will help this team contend for a Champions League crown, which is still the goal. Yamal keeps goingWeirdly, last season was a down season for Lamine Yamal as he missed time with injuries and was "only" involved in 27 LaLiga goals. Now he has scored eight and assisted six more in only nine games played as he's reaching yet another level. There are too many superlatives to describe what he's doing on the pitch, but his dribbling, vision and finishing are off the charts. 

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            In Champions League play, he took a Galatasaray defender for a ride along the sideline before setting up Anthony Gordon for a goal, and with how much talent is around him, Barcelona can maximize what Yamal does well. 
Yamal is already a Ballon d'Or contender, and the fact that he's still improving his game means the rest of the world will need to look out. He's already doing things that haven't been done by anyone who isn't named Lionel Messi, and we're only scratching the surface of this potential. Sometimes players who break out at such a young age can plateau and stay at the same level for years, but when you're seeing clear improvement from him in a juggernaut of a team, anything could happen here. Even a perfect season -- it's too early to talk about one yet, but it could happen.
Strikers on strikersEven though he hasn't played in three games, it wouldn't be right to talk about Barcelona without mentioning the exploits of Raphinha and his position change. Flick has pushed him centrally to be a striker, and it has worked to perfection. He's leading the European Golden Shoe rankings for the top scorer across Europe's leagues, and you'd think that he has been a striker for his entire career. It's impressive management from Flick, and with Gabriel Jesus as the backup, the squad isn't missing a step even without their star man in the middle. It helps keep up the attacking pressure, and with a Clasico against Real Madrid looming next week, Barcelona can turn all of this into a commanding lead in LaLiga.

schema.headline: How good can Barcelona be? Eleven wins straight and counting to start the season - CBS Sports

title: Eagles to place Jalen Hurts on IR, as he deals with superficial blood clot, per report - CBS Sports
description: Hurts is out indefinitely and will miss the game against the Panthers on Sunday, and at least three more
body:
Hurts is out indefinitely and will miss the game against the Panthers on Sunday, and at least three more
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:05 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles are placing quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is out this week with a superficial blood clot, on injured reserve, the team officially announced on Saturday, after consultations with numerous doctors and experts. Going on IR sidelines a player for at least four weeks, meaning Hurts will miss this weekend's game, as the team previously announced, along with three divisional games.He will miss matchups against the Carolina Panthers, Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders and New York Giants. Hurts will be eligible to return against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22, but that doesn't mean he is guaranteed to be back then. With Hurts out, Tanner McKee will be leading the offense, and rookie Cole Payton will be the backup. The Eagles released a statement saying Hurts requested treatment on his calf four days after their Week 4 loss against the Los Angeles Rams. The Eagles performed an ultrasound on his leg after they landed in London for their game against the Jacksonville Jaguars and found the superficial blood clot. The team's medical staff determined he could play, and the team conducted a follow-up ultrasound where they found the blood clot had moved, which can lead to a serious health situation. 
When he can play will be determined by his medical team, meaning he could miss more than just four games. Hurts is still working on the best treatment plan for the situation and the team believes it is treatable. Hurts and the team are both still looking into more options and are putting the quarterback's health as top priority. 
        
            
                Jalen Hurts blood clot: Expert weighs in on Eagles' situation, and when QB could return to the field
                
                    Jordan Dajani                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Blood thinners are a main treatment for blood clots and a player cannot play while on that medication. Typically, a patient would be on blood thinners for six weeks, but if the clot is minor, it may be treatable with other measures, such as anti-inflammatories. If the clot worsens, it could mean more time on blood thinners, which would, in turn, mean more time away from the field. 
The Eagles added some security in the quarterback position this week, signing Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys practice squad.

schema.headline: Eagles to place Jalen Hurts on IR, as he deals with superficial blood clot, per report - CBS Sports
